# `silk/mem/any_box`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Owned heap storage for a value behind an erased interface contract.

## When to use
Use [`AnyBox`](#AnyBox) when a struct, collection, or task must own a heterogeneous value satisfying an
interface contract (`any Interface`, optionally with `+ Transferable` and `+ Concurrent`), and
a borrowed `&any Interface` or `&mut any Interface` reference cannot live long enough. Use
`silk.mem.box.Box` when the concrete type is fixed at compile time.

## Details
[`AnyBox.make`](#AnyBox.impl.make) allocates space for one concrete value `C` through [`Allocator`](./mem-allocator.md#Allocator), moves `C`
into that allocation, and returns `AnyBox<E>` holding the concrete type's runtime tag and owned
allocation. [`get`](#AnyBox.impl.get) and [`getMut`](#AnyBox.impl.getMut) borrow the stored value as `&E` and `&mut E` for interface
dispatch. [`narrow`](#AnyBox.impl.narrow) converts an `AnyBox<From>` into an `AnyBox<To>` in place when `From`
satisfies `To` without reallocating.

`AnyBox<E>` is affine (never `Copy`). Dropping an `AnyBox<E>` runs the stored concrete type's
`Drop` cleanup before releasing its allocation. `AnyBox<E>` is `Transferable` if and only if
`E` carries `+ Transferable`, and `Concurrent` if and only if `E` carries `+ Concurrent`.

## Errors
[`AnyBox.make`](#AnyBox.impl.make) fails with [`OutOfMemoryError`](./mem-allocator.md#OutOfMemoryError) if [`Allocator.allocate`](./mem-allocator.md#Allocator.allocate) cannot supply
storage for the concrete value.

## Examples
### Store different implementations of an interface in one list
```silk
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.mem.any_box { AnyBox }

interface Named {
  fn code(self: &Self) -> i32
}

struct Left {}
struct Right { offset: i32 }

impl Named for Left {
  fn code(self: &Self) -> i32 {
    return 20
  }
}

impl Named for Right {
  fn code(self: &Self) -> i32 {
    return 20 + self.offset
  }
}

effect fn program() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut items = List<AnyBox<any Named>>.make()
  run List<AnyBox<any Named>>.append(
    &mut items,
    run AnyBox<any Named>.make(Left {}) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator),
  ) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  run List<AnyBox<any Named>>.append(
    &mut items,
    run AnyBox<any Named>.make(Right { offset: 2 }) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator),
  ) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let slice = List<AnyBox<any Named>>.asSlice(&items)
  let total = slice[0].get().code() + slice[1].get().code()
  if total != 42 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn outOfMemory(error: OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  return 1
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  return run Effect.catchAll(program(), outOfMemory)
}
```

Import as `AnyBox` with `import silk.mem.any_box { AnyBox }`.

## `AnyBox`

```silk
pub struct AnyBox<E>
```

An owned heap box holding one value erased behind interface contract `E`.

### When to use

Use `AnyBox<E>` when you need to move, store, or return an owned heterogeneous value whose
type implements `E` (such as `any Component` or `any Task + Transferable`).

### Details

`E` must be an erased interface contract (`any I`, with optional `+ Transferable` and
`+ Concurrent`). An `AnyBox<E>` holds a tag identifying the concrete type and one allocation
storing that value. When the `AnyBox<E>` is dropped, it runs the concrete value's `Drop`
logic before releasing the allocation.

`AnyBox<E>` is never `Copy`. It satisfies `Transferable` when `E` requires `+ Transferable`,
and `Concurrent` when `E` requires `+ Concurrent`.

### Gotchas

`AnyBox<E>` rejects non-erased type arguments (such as `AnyBox<i32>`). The concrete type
passed to [`AnyBox.make`](#AnyBox.impl.make) must satisfy all interface and thread-safety bounds named in `E`.

<a id="AnyBox.impl"></a>

## Implementation `AnyBox<E>`

```silk
impl<E> AnyBox<E>
```

<a id="AnyBox.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub effect fn make<C>(value: C) -> AnyBox<E>
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Allocates space through [`Allocator`](./mem-allocator.md#Allocator) and moves `value` into a new `AnyBox<E>`.

#### Details

Requests `Layout.of<C>()` from `&mut Allocator` and stores `value` alongside the runtime
tag for `C` under erased contract `E`. Dropping the returned `AnyBox<E>` drops `value` and
releases the allocation.

#### Errors

- [`OutOfMemoryError`](./mem-allocator.md#OutOfMemoryError) when the allocator cannot supply storage for `C`. No value is leaked.

#### Gotchas

`C` must implement every interface in `E`, plus `Transferable` and `Concurrent` if `E`
includes those bounds. Calling `AnyBox<E>.make` with a type `C` that does not satisfy `E`
fails compilation.

<a id="AnyBox.impl.get"></a>

### Method `get`

```silk
pub fn get(self: &Self) -> &E
```

Borrows the boxed value as a shared erased interface reference `&E`.

#### Details

The returned reference shares `self`'s borrow lifetime and dispatches interface methods
dynamically to the boxed concrete value without allocating.

<a id="AnyBox.impl.getMut"></a>

### Method `getMut`

```silk
pub fn getMut(self: &mut Self) -> &mut E
```

Borrows the boxed value as an exclusive erased interface reference `&mut E`.

#### Details

The returned reference borrows `self` exclusively so interface methods taking `&mut Self` can
mutate the boxed value in place without reallocating.

<a id="AnyBox.impl.narrow"></a>

### Method `narrow`

```silk
pub fn narrow<To>(self: Self) -> AnyBox<To>
```

Narrows this `AnyBox<E>` into an `AnyBox<To>` without moving the underlying allocation.

#### Details

Preserves the concrete value's tag and heap allocation while changing the static contract
from `E` to `To`. `To` must be an erased interface contract whose interfaces and thread-safety
bounds are already required by `E`.

#### Gotchas

Narrowing to a contract `To` with requirements that `E` does not guarantee fails
compilation.
